description: Hand-curated oracle for minor-key Roman numeral & mode reconciliation. Each case has expected values written by reading music theory, NOT generated by the analyzer. These cases are the gate for fixes to token_converter.py and unified_pattern_service._detect_mode_label.
schema_notes: key: expected key the analyzer should report
key_hint (optional): if present, passed to analyzer as input — use sparingly to isolate roman-numeral logic from key-detection ambiguity
roman_numerals: exact expected sequence after bug fixes; minor-key convention follows current codebase (III/VI without flats, ♭VII with flat) — convention reform is out of scope
mode_expected (optional): if present, analyzer must report this exact mode label
mode_must_not_be (optional): list of mode labels the analyzer must NOT report
comment: music-theory rationale for the expected values, written for the next person who has to debug this

progressions.name: user_em_progression_full
progressions.comment: Reported by user on 2026-05-06. Three bugs visible: (1) E7 is V7/iv (E-G#-B-D, dominant); old code emits 'i7' because major-quality upgrade only fires at V — must become I7. (2) Bbdim is a tritone-rooted chromatic passing chord between two V7s — must be ♭v° (or ♯iv°), NOT ♭VI (♭VI of E minor is C, not B♭). (3) Mode was reported as 'E Dorian' — impossible: Cmaj7/Am7/Am6 contain C natural; Dorian needs C#. iv6 (Am6 = A-C-E-F#) is labeled iv pending future 6th-quality detection.

progressions.name: secondary_V7_iv_in_e_minor
progressions.comment: Minimal isolation of the V7/iv bug. E7 is unambiguously a major-third dominant (G♯ in chord); must NOT be 'i7'. Whether to label I7 vs V7/iv is a separate enhancement — we accept I7 as the immediate post-fix output.

progressions.name: secondary_V7_iv_in_a_minor
progressions.comment: Same bug as previous, transposed to A minor — proves the fix is key-agnostic, not E-specific.

progressions.name: chromatic_passing_dim_in_e_minor
progressions.comment: Isolated test for the Bbdim→♭VI bug. Bb is 6 semitones (tritone) above E; minor_romans[6] currently says 'bVI' which is wrong — ♭VI is at 8 semitones (=C). Tritone slot should be ♭v° or ♯iv°. Also tests dim/° detection in seventh-quality block (currently absent).

progressions.name: chromatic_passing_dim_in_c_major
progressions.comment: Major-key chromatic passing diminished between I and ii. C#dim is technically ♯i°, but enharmonic respelling is out of scope; ♭ii° is the post-fix expected output (semitone 1 → 'bII' from major_romans + ° suffix from dim detection). key_hint isolates this from the unrelated key-detection ambiguity (without a hint the analyzer flips to C minor on this chord set).

progressions.name: pure_aeolian_minimal
progressions.comment: i-v-i with diatonic minor v (B-D-F♯ = Bm, F♯ from natural minor scale). Insufficient evidence for any specific mode beyond minor — must NOT auto-classify as Dorian (which would require C♯, absent here).

progressions.name: aeolian_with_bvii_no_dorian_signature
progressions.comment: The smoking-gun case for the mode-detection bug. ♭VII alone does NOT prove Dorian — Aeolian, Mixolydian, and Dorian all have natural ♭VII. The Dorian signature is the RAISED 6th (C♯ in E Dorian), which is absent here. Current code flips to Dorian on ♭VII presence — that's the bug.

progressions.name: legitimate_d_dorian_positive_control
progressions.comment: POSITIVE control: this SHOULD classify as Dorian. G major in D minor contains B natural — that's #6, the Dorian signature. If the fix accidentally over-corrects and never emits Dorian, this test catches it.

progressions.name: legitimate_g_mixolydian_positive_control
progressions.comment: POSITIVE control for Mixolydian. F natural in G major is ♭7, the Mixolydian signature. Confirms the mode-detection fix doesn't regress legitimate modal classifications.

progressions.name: e_harmonic_minor_cadence
progressions.comment: Textbook minor-key authentic cadence. B7 contains D♯ (raised 7), the harmonic-minor leading tone. Sanity check: this should not break under any of our fixes.

progressions.name: c_minor_classical_cadence
progressions.comment: Same cadence transposed to C minor — different position checks for table-index bugs in token_converter.

progressions.name: andalusian_in_a_minor
progressions.comment: Classic Andalusian/flamenco cadence. E (not Em) is the harmonic-minor V. NOTE: codebase emits 'VI' (no flat) at semitone 8 and '♭VII' (with flat) at semitone 10 — that's an internal convention inconsistency, but cleaning it up is out of scope here. Asserting current convention so this test isolates the bugs we ARE fixing.

progressions.name: major_basic_authentic_sanity
progressions.comment: The simplest possible major-key cadence. If this breaks under our fixes, we've over-corrected something. Pure regression guard.

progressions.name: major_50s_progression_sanity
progressions.comment: I-vi-IV-V doo-wop. Without a key hint the analyzer flips to C MINOR (the four chords are diatonic to either, and the heuristic guesses minor — that's a separate key-detection bug). key_hint isolates the token-converter logic: tests that vi (minor triad at interval 9 in major) is correctly lowercased and not given a flat prefix.

progressions.name: major_50s_progression_no_hint
progressions.comment: Same progression with the resolving C — should make C-major detection more reliable without a hint. If this passes but the previous case fails, we have a key-detection issue that's separate from token-converter / mode-reconciliation. Documents that gap explicitly.
